title: Oppenheimer's Gita quote originally 'I am time'

tellings.quote: reading that the original translation was not I am death the destroyer of worlds. It was I am time the destroyer of worlds.
Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom, The Slayer Time, Ancient of Days, come hither to consume;

plain: The famous line that J. Robert Oppenheimer, the physicist who led the building of the first atomic bomb, took from the Hindu scripture the Bhagavad Gita, "I am death, the destroyer of worlds", originally read "I am time, the destroyer of worlds". A guest named Dave Rossi tells Michels he read this, and it would mean the scripture speaks of time itself as the destroyer. He does not say which translation he read; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 English translation, The Song Celestial, the god Krishna says at chapter 11, verse 32, "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom", which speaks of Time, though in other words.

discussion.by: The Song Celestial, or Bhagavad-Gita (translated by Edwin Arnold)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which translation he read; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 translation read here, Krishna's words at chapter 11, verse 32 are "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom", which speaks of Time as the teller says, in other words than "I am time, the destroyer of worlds".
